source: Stark Road Gospel Hall recent service announcements (spoken hymn numbers + first lines as commonly sung)
note: Numbers as spoken at SRGH. Verify against classic BHB / GHB; if GHB, book=ghb. Non-PD hymns stay indexed with zero lyrics in stanza/pair files.

hymns.first_line_en: What can wash away my sin?
hymns.author: Robert Lowry
hymns.notes: Gospel hymn often called as #23 at SRGH; GHB numbering. Lowry d.1899 — PD.

hymns.first_line_en: I stand amazed in the presence
hymns.author: Charles H. Gabriel

hymns.first_line_en: Come, for the feast is spread
hymns.common_title: Yet There Is Room / Come hear the gospel sound
hymns.author: Horatius Bonar
hymns.notes: Gospel invitation hymn; Bonar PD. First line variants exist in gospel hymnals.

hymns.first_line_en: We've a story to tell to the nations
hymns.common_title: We've a Story to Tell to the Nations
hymns.author: H. Ernest Nichol
hymns.notes: Published 1896; gospel tidings hymn as announced. US PD for 1896 publication.

hymns.first_line_en: O soul, are you weary and troubled?
hymns.author: Helen Howarth Lemmel
hymns.exclude_reason: Helen Howarth Lemmel d.1961 — not public domain. Index only; zero lyrics in train.
hymns.notes: Do not put lyrics in stanza or pair files.

hymns.first_line_en: My faith has found a resting place
hymns.common_title: My Faith Has Found a Resting Place
hymns.author: Eliza E. Hewitt
hymns.notes: Late 19th-c. gospel hymn; Hewitt d.1920 — PD.

hymns.first_line_en: One there is above all others
hymns.alt_first_line_en: One there is who loves thee
hymns.common_title: One There Is Above All Others
hymns.author: John Newton
hymns.notes: Newton text; brethren assemblies often announce a related first-line variant.
